[[File:Mount Haku from Onanjimine 2011-07-17.jpg|thumb|right|300px|{{ill|Mount Haku|ja|白山|lt=Mount Haku|lt_ja=白山}}]]
{{nihongo|'''Kikurihime no Kami'''|菊理媛神}}, also known as {{nihongo|'''Kikurihime no Mikoto'''|菊理媛命}} (read ''Kukurihime'' or ''Kikurihime''), is a Japanese {{ill|Shinto|ja|神道|lt=Shinto|lt_ja=神道}} {{ill|Kami|ja|神|lt=goddess|lt_ja=神}}<ref name="sev1">''Shintō Daijiten'', vol. 1 (Heibonsha, 1937), frame 264 (original p. 455), "Kukurihime no Mikoto".</ref><ref name="eotwgKikurihime">Matsumura Kazuo et al. (eds.), ''Sekai Megami Daijiten'' (Hara Shobō, 2015), pp. 42–43, "Kukurihime".</ref> identified with {{nihongo|'''Shirayama Hime no Kami'''|白山比咩神|しらやまひめのかみ}}, who is worshipped on {{ill|Mount Haku|ja|白山|lt=Mount Haku|lt_ja=白山}} in {{ill|Kaga Province|ja|加賀国|lt=Kaga Province|lt_ja=加賀国}}<ref>Machida Sōhō, ''Yama no Reiryoku'' (Kōdansha, 2003), pp. 177–178.</ref> and at the {{ill|Hakusan shrine|ja|白山信仰|lt=Hakusan shrines|lt_ja=白山神社}} throughout Japan, headed by {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|ja|白山比咩神社|lt=Shirayama Hime Shrine|lt_ja=白山比咩神社}} in {{ill|Hakusan, Ishikawa|ja|白山市|lt=Hakusan|lt_ja=白山市}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture|lt_ja=石川県}}.<ref name="sev1"/><ref name="ekdc">Kōkoku Keishinkai (ed.), ''Zenkoku Yūmei Jinja Goshashinchō'' (December 1922), "Kokuhei Chūsha Shirayama Hime Jinja", National Diet Library Digital Collection.</ref><ref name="mdfdd">Yabe Zenzō, ''Shoshin Shinmei Saijin Jiten'' (Tenbōsha, 1991), pp. 446–447, "Shirayama Hime Jinja".</ref> She is mentioned in the ''Nihon Shoki'', but not in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|lt=Kojiki|lt_ja=古事記}}''.<ref name="Tonerishin'nō-hen">''Nihon Shoki'' vol. 1, National Diet Library Digital Collection.</ref><ref name="hakusenfestival">Kaburagi Seiki, ''Hakusan Saijin Kō'' (1922), frame 9 (original p. 8).</ref> She mediated between {{ill|Izanagi|ja|イザナギ|lt=Izanagi|lt_ja=伊奘諾尊}} and {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|lt=Izanami|lt_ja=伊弉冉尊}} after Izanagi fled from {{ill|Yomi|ja|黄泉|lt=Yomi|lt_ja=黄泉}}, the land of the dead.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Kawaguchi |first1=Kenji |title=Nihon no Kamisama Yomitoki Jiten |date=2012 |publisher=Kashiwa Shobō}}</ref> She is also venerated at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|ja|靖国神社|lt=Yasukuni Shrine|lt_ja=靖国神社}} in {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|lt=Tokyo|lt_ja=東京}} and at {{ill|Yōrō Shrine|ja|養老神社|lt=Yōrō Shrine|lt_ja=養老神社}} in {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ja|岐阜県|lt=Gifu Prefecture|lt_ja=岐阜県}}.<ref name="popshinto"/><ref name="histshinto"/> Despite her brief appearance, her popularity is shown by her worship at some 3,000 {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|lt=shrines|lt_ja=神社}} across Japan.<ref name="popshinto">Brian Bocking, ''A Popular Dictionary of Shinto'' (Routledge, 2005).</ref><ref name="histshinto">Stuart D. B. Picken, ''Historical Dictionary of Shinto'' (Scarecrow Press, 2010) p.&nbsp;102.</ref> Under {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|ja|神仏習合|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō|lt_ja=神仏習合}} she was later identified with {{ill|Kannon|ja|観音菩薩|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|lt_ja=観音菩薩}}.<ref name="popshinto"/><ref name="histshinto"/><ref name="msp">Machida, ''Yama no Reiryoku'', p. 180.</ref>

== Kikurihime in myth ==
In {{ill|Japanese mythology|ja|日本神話|lt=Japanese mythology|lt_ja=日本神話}} she does not appear in the ''Kojiki'' or in the main text of the ''Nihon Shoki''; she appears only once, in a variant (the tenth "alternative writing", ''aru fumi'') of the ''Nihon Shoki''.<ref name="Tonerishin'nō-hen"/><ref name="hakusenfestival"/>

{{Quotation|
'''Original text'''

{{lang|ja|及其与妹相闘於泉平坂也、伊奘諾尊曰、始為族悲、及思哀者、是吾之怯矣。時泉守道者白云、有言矣。曰、吾与汝已生国矣。奈何更求生乎。吾則当留此国、不可共去。是時、菊理媛神亦有白事。伊奘諾尊聞而善之。乃散去矣。}}
}}
{{Quotation|
'''Translation'''

When he quarrelled with his wife (Izanami) at Yomotsu Hirasaka, Izanagi said: "That I at first grieved and longed for her was because I was weak."

Then the Yomotsuchimoribito (the guardian of the road to Yomi) spoke: "There is a message from Izanami. She says: 'I have already borne the land with you. Why should you seek still more births? I shall stay in this land, and cannot go back with you.'"

At this time Kukurihime also had something to say. Izanagi heard it and praised it. Then he went away.
}}

Izanagi visited Yomi to meet {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|lt=Izanami|lt_ja=伊弉冉尊}}, who had died in the {{ill|Kamiumi|ja|神産み|lt=birth of the gods|lt_ja=神産み}}, but on seeing her changed form he fled.<ref name="sev1"/><ref>Ujitani Tsutomu, ''Nihon Shoki: Zen Gendaigo-yaku'', vol. 1 (Kōdansha, 1988), pp. 32–33.</ref> She caught up with him at Yomotsu Hirasaka ({{ill|Yomotsu Hirasaka|ja|黄泉比良坂|lt=Yomotsu Hirasaka|lt_ja=黄泉比良坂}}) and they argued.<ref>Iida Teiji (ed.), ''Shin'yaku Nihon Shoki'' (Sūzanbō, 1912), pp. 45–46.</ref><ref name="iwanami56">Sakamoto Tarō et al. (eds.), ''Nihon Shoki'', vol. 1 (Iwanami Bunko, 1994), pp. 56–57.</ref> The Yomotsuchimoribito then appeared<ref>Inoue Tetsujirō and Ueda Kazutoshi (supervisors), ''Suika Shintō'', vol. 1 (Shun'yōdō, 1935), frame 237 (original p. 431).</ref> and relayed Izanami's words that she could not go back with him.<ref name="tanabe">Tanabe Katsuya, ''Nihon Shoki Kōgi: Jindai no Maki'' (Teikoku Jingikai, 1932), frame 63 (original p. 117).</ref> Kikurihime then appeared and said something, and Izanagi praised what both the Yomotsuchimoribito and Kikurihime had said, and went home.<ref name="uematsu">Uematsu Yasushi, ''Kana Nihon Shoki'', vol. 1 (Daidōkan Shoten, 1920), frames 92–93 (original pp. 36–38).</ref><ref name="tanabe"/> What she said is not recorded, nor is anything said about her origins.<ref name="uematsu"/><ref>Kanai Nanryū, ''Kamigami no Mokushiroku'' (Tokuma Shoten, 1980), pp. 75–77.</ref>

Because in this story she is taken to have reconciled Izanagi and Izanami, Kikurihime is regarded as a deity of {{ill|En-musubi|ja|縁結び|lt=marriage and good relationships|lt_ja=縁結び}}. Other views make her a goddess serving Izanami in Yomi;<ref name="tanabe"/><ref name="hirata">Hirata Atsutane, ''Tama no Mihashira'', annotated by Koyasu Nobukuni (Iwanami Bunko, 1987), pp. 72–73.</ref> a daughter of Izanagi and Izanami;<ref name="hakusenfestival"/> the "god of Yomi" (''Yomotsukami'') with whom Izanami says in the ''Kojiki'' she will consult about returning, that is, the great god of Yomi before Izanami;<ref>Kurano Kenji (ed.), ''Kojiki'' (Iwanami Bunko, 1963), pp. 26–28.</ref><ref>Tsugita Masaki, ''Kojiki: Zen'yakuchū'', vol. 1 (Kōdansha, 1977), p. 65.</ref><ref>Saigō Nobutsuna, ''Kojiki Chūshaku'', vol. 1 (Heibonsha, 1975), p. 176.</ref><ref>Hirata, ''Tama no Mihashira'', p. 73, note 10.</ref> the {{ill|Aramitama|ja|荒魂|lt=aramitama|lt_ja=荒魂}} or {{ill|Nigimitama|ja|和魂|lt=nigimitama|lt_ja=和魂}} of Izanami;<ref name="hakusenfestival"/> or another name for Izanami herself.<ref name="suika238">''Suika Shintō'', vol. 1, frame 238 (original p. 432).</ref><ref>Kanai, ''Kamigami no Mokushiroku'', pp. 89–92.</ref> In any case Kikurihime (and the Yomotsuchimoribito) is closely bound up with Izanagi and Izanami.<ref name="suika238"/><ref>Kaburagi, ''Hakusan Saijin Kō'', frame 11 (original p. 12).</ref> Because she mediated between the dead (Izanami) and the living (Izanagi), some suggest she is a goddess of {{ill|Shamanism|ja|シャーマニズム|lt=shamans|lt_ja=シャーマン}} ({{ill|Miko|ja|巫女|lt=miko|lt_ja=巫女}}). She is also held to be a deity who purifies {{ill|Kegare|ja|穢れ|lt=kegare|lt_ja=ケガレ}}.<ref>''Suika Shintō'', vol. 1, frames 237–238 (original pp. 431–432).</ref>

=== Name ===
''Kukuri'' in the name is thought to mean "to bind together" (括り), from her bringing Izanagi and Izanami together.<ref name="sev1"/><ref name="seten86">Sekai Seiten Zenshū Kankōkai (ed.), ''Sekai Seiten Zenshū'', first series vol. 1, ''Nihon Shoki Jindai no Maki'' (1920), frame 86 (original p. 87).</ref> Some say the character for {{ill|Chrysanthemum|ja|キク|lt=chrysanthemum|lt_ja=菊花}} (菊) was used for ''kukuru'' because the old name of the chrysanthemum was ''kuku'',<ref>''Sekai Megami Daijiten'', pp. 42–43.</ref> others that it comes from the shape of the flower.<ref name="seten86"/> One theory reads the old pronunciation of 菊 as ''kokoro'' and calls her "Kokorohime".<ref name="iwanami56"/> Other theories connect the name with spinning thread (binding), take it as ''kukuri''/''kuguru'' ("to dive"), making her a water deity, or derive it from ''kikiireru'' ("to hear and accept").<ref name="uematsu"/><ref name="suika238"/> The Hakusan Shrine at Yanagida, {{ill|Noto, Ishikawa|ja|能登町|lt=Noto|lt_ja=能登町}}, {{ill|Hōsu District, Ishikawa|ja|鳳珠郡|lt=Hōsu District|lt_ja=鳳珠郡}}, writes the name 久久理姫命 (also 久々利姫命).<ref>''Shintō Daijiten'', vol. 2 (Heibonsha, 1939), frame 119 (original p. 200).</ref><ref>[http://www.ishikawa-jinjacho.or.jp/ Ishikawa Prefecture Jinjachō], Hakusan Shrine (Yanagida, Noto).</ref>

== Kikurihime in worship ==
How she came to be identified with Shirayama Hime is unknown. At one time books named the deities of {{ill|Shirayama Hime Shrine|ja|白山比咩神社|lt=Shirayama Hime Shrine|lt_ja=白山比咩神社}}, the head shrine of the Hakusan shrines, as Izanagi and Izanami. The first to make Kikurihime the deity of Hakusan is said to have been {{ill|Ōe no Masafusa|ja|大江匡房|lt=Ōe no Masafusa|lt_ja=大江匡房}} (1041–1111), in the ''{{ill|Fusō Meigetsushū|ja|扶桑明月集|lt=Fusō Meigetsushū|lt_ja=扶桑明月集}}''.<ref>"Hakutōsan to Hakusan shinkō ni tsuite (ge)", ''Higashi Ajia no Kodai Bunka'' no. 49 (Daiwa Shobō, autumn 1986), p. 204.</ref> Hakusan was a {{ill|Sacred mountain|ja|霊山|lt=sacred mountain|lt_ja=霊山}} and {{ill|Reijō|ja|霊場|lt=mountain pilgrimage site|lt_ja=山岳霊場}} with a following centred on the {{ill|Hokuriku region|ja|北陸地方|lt=Hokuriku region|lt_ja=北陸地方}}.<ref>Okada Shōji (ed.), ''Nihon Shintōshi'' (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2010), p. 300.</ref>

The ''Keiran Shūyōshū'', written by a Tendai monk in the fourteenth century, quotes the ''Fusō Meigetsushū'' on the eight princes (Hachiōji) descending beside the great rock of Kono-Higashiyama in Shiga District, Ōmi, and on {{ill|Hakusan Myōri Gongen|ja|白山妙理権現|lt=Hakusan Myōri Gongen|lt_ja=白山妙理権現}} appearing at the foot of Hachiōji when the Marōdo-no-miya descended in the first year of Enryaku under {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇|lt=Emperor Kanmu|lt_ja=桓武天皇}}.

The ''{{ill|Twenty-Two Shrines|ja|二十二社|lt=Nijūnisha Chūshiki|lt_ja=二十二社註式}}'', said to have been compiled by {{ill|Yoshida Kanetomo|ja|吉田兼倶|lt=Yoshida Kanetomo|lt_ja=吉田兼倶}} in {{ill|Bunmei (era)|ja|文明 (日本)|lt=Bunmei|lt_ja=文明}} 1 (1469), quotes the ''Fusō Meigetsushū'' as saying that the Marōdo-no-miya, which descended at the foot of Hachiōji in Enryaku 1, is Hakusan, "that is, Kukurihime". The ''{{ill|Dai Nihon Ichinomiya Ki|ja|大日本一宮記|lt=Dai Nihon Ichinomiya Ki|lt_ja=大日本一宮記}}'' names Kikurihime as the deity of the upper shrine of Shirayama Hime Shrine.

Books of the Edo period then state outright that Shirayama Hime and Kikurihime are one deity.<ref>How the identification came about in the Edo period is discussed in Yamagishi, "Hakusan shinkō to Kaga Baba", ''Sangaku Shūkyōshi Kenkyū Sōsho'' 10.</ref>

Under {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|ja|神仏習合|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō|lt_ja=神仏習合}}, Shirayama Hime was called '''{{ill|Hakusan Daigongen|ja|白山大権現|lt=Hakusan Daigongen|lt_ja=白山大権現}}''', '''{{ill|Hakusan Myōri Gongen|ja|白山妙理権現|lt=Hakusan Myōri Gongen|lt_ja=白山妙理権現}}'''<ref name="ryakushi">Saitō Hideo (ed.), ''Shirayama Hime Jinja Ryakushi'' (1922), frames 4–5 (original pp. 1–2).</ref> or '''Hakusan Myōri Bosatsu''', and her {{ill|Honji suijaku|ja|本地垂迹説|lt=honji|lt_ja=本地仏}} was the '''{{ill|Eleven-faced Kannon|ja|十一面観音|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|lt_ja=十一面観音}}''',<ref name="msp"/> though there were various other views.<ref>Kaburagi, ''Hakusan Saijin Kō'', frames 5–8 (original pp. 1–6).</ref>

Today Shirayama Hime Shrine has Kikurihime (Shirayama Hime) as its principal deity,<ref>''Shintō Daijiten'', vol. 2, frame 119 (original pp. 200–201).</ref> with Izanagi and Izanami enshrined beside her.<ref>Tsurugi Hoshōkai (ed.), ''Tsurugi Annai'' (1936), "Shirayama Hime Jinja", National Diet Library Digital Collection.</ref><ref name="ryakushi"/>

The ''Gyokusenshū'' records that Kikurihime (Izanami) is enshrined at {{ill|Kumano Hongū Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社|lt=Kumano Hongū Taisha|lt_ja=熊野本宮大社}}.<ref name="suika238"/><ref>Hayakawa Junzaburō (ed.), ''Shintō Sōsho'' (Kokusho Kankōkai, 1911), "Kukurihime no Den", p. 148.</ref>
